diff --git a/outlines/types/__init__.py b/outlines/types/__init__.py
index 85af9adc..27ff12c0 100644
--- a/outlines/types/__init__.py
+++ b/outlines/types/__init__.py
@@ -59,6 +59,16 @@ email = Regex(
     r"""(?:[a-z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+(?:\.[a-z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+)*|"(?:[\x01-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x21\x23-\x5b\x5d-\x7f]|\\[\x01-\x09\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x7f])*")@(?:(?:[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?\.)+[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?|\[(?:(?:(2(5[0-5]|[0-4][0-9])|1[0-9][0-9]|[1-9]?[0-9]))\.){3}(?:(2(5[0-5]|[0-4][0-9])|1[0-9][0-9]|[1-9]?[0-9])|[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9]:(?:[\x01-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x21-\x5a\x53-\x7f]|\\[\x01-\x09\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x7f])+)\])"""
 )
 
+# Matches a 16-digit credit card number written as four groups of four digits,
+# with no separators, with spaces only, or with hyphens only. Mixing the two
+# separators (1234-5678 9012-3456) is refused, so the alternatives are spelled
+# out instead of using a backreference, which no finite automaton can follow.
+# [0-9] rather than \d keeps other scripts' digits out. Like the ISBN pattern
+# below, it checks the format only, not the Luhn check digit.
+credit_card = Regex(
+    r"[0-9]{4}(-[0-9]{4}){3}|[0-9]{4}( [0-9]{4}){3}|[0-9]{16}"
+)
+
 # Matches any ISBN number. Note that this is not completely correct as not all
 # 10 or 13 digits numbers are valid ISBNs. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISBN
 # Taken from O'Reilly's Regular Expression Cookbook:
@@ -68,3 +78,23 @@ email = Regex(
 isbn = Regex(
     r"(?:ISBN(?:-1[03])?:? )?(?=[0-9X]{10}$|(?=(?:[0-9]+[- ]){3})[- 0-9X]{13}$|97[89][0-9]{10}$|(?=(?:[0-9]+[- ]){4})[- 0-9]{17}$)(?:97[89][- ]?)?[0-9]{1,5}[- ]?[0-9]+[- ]?[0-9]+[- ]?[0-9X]"
 )
+
+# Matches HTTP and HTTPS web URLs: the scheme, a host, an optional port, and an
+# optional path, query string and fragment. The host is a domain name (labels of
+# letters, digits and inner hyphens, ending in a label that starts with a letter,
+# so "localhost" and "a.co" match but "1.2.3.4.5" does not), an IPv4 address
+# whose four numbers are 0 to 255, or an IPv6 address in brackets (checked only
+# for its characters). The port is 0 to 65535. The path, query and fragment take
+# any character but white space, so a URL with a space never matches. The
+# pattern uses no look-around, which the regex engines that guide generation
+# do not support.
+url = Regex(
+    r"https?://"
+    r"(([a-zA-Z0-9]([a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\.)*[a-zA-Z]([a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?"
+    r"|((25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9][0-9]|[1-9]?[0-9])\.){3}(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9][0-9]|[1-9]?[0-9])"
+    r"|\[[0-9a-fA-F:.]*:[0-9a-fA-F:.]*\])"
+    r"(:([0-9]{1,4}|[1-5][0-9]{4}|6[0-4][0-9]{3}|65[0-4][0-9]{2}|655[0-2][0-9]|6553[0-5]))?"
+    r"(/[^\s?#]*)?"
+    r"(\?[^\s#]*)?"
+    r"(#[^\s]*)?"
+)
